meta.topStoryHeadline: Thelma Golden to Step Down from the Studio Museum in 2027
meta.topStorySummary: The museum begins a leadership search as Golden prepares to leave in late 2027, following two decades championing Black artists.
executiveSummary: Thanksgiving weekend brings the African Diaspora International Film Festival, Complexions’ final Joyce performances, and Samson et Dalila with Morris Robinson and Alfred Walker at the Met.
Ailey opens at New York City Center on December 2. Seven Guitars is now playing at Lincoln Center Theater, while Florence Price’s music features with the New York Philharmonic through December 1.

Thelma Golden plans a Studio Museum leadership transition for late 2027. Lawrence Brownlee and Cincinnati Opera’s Black Opera Project receive international honors, and National Black Theatre celebrates support for its new home and artist residencies.

December brings Victory Boyd at the Billie, poetry at the Poetry Project, new gallery discoveries, and family Kwanzaa programming. Calvin Royal III returns to New York on January 21, with additional ABT performances in March.

events.title: 34th African Diaspora International Film Festival
events.venue: Teachers College, Columbia; The Forum at Columbia; Cinema Village; some films online
events.description: More than seventy films explore Black life across the diaspora. The November 28 opening gala presents John Johnson Reporting, narrated by Whoopi Goldberg, with a conversation featuring Johnson and WNBC’s David Ushery. Check the festival schedule for venues and times.
events.price: $15 screenings; $60 Fan or Virtual passes; $300 All-Access; gala tickets priced separately

events.title: Complexions Contemporary Ballet: Homecoming Season
events.description: Founded by Dwight Rhoden and Desmond Richardson; world premieres by Rhoden, Tommie-Waheed Evans, and Jillian Davis. Desmond Richardson, ABT's first African American principal dancer, co-leads a company built on dancers of every background. Three programs.

events.title: Samson et Dalila — Morris Robinson and Alfred Walker
events.description: Morris Robinson sings the Old Hebrew throughout the run of Saint-Saëns’s biblical opera. Alfred Walker appears as Abimélech on every date except December 15. Aigul Akhmetshina and Clay Hilley lead the cast as Dalila and Samson, conducted by Giacomo Sagripanti.
events.price: From $33 including fees; varies by performance and seat

events.title: Ailey at New York City Center
events.description: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater returns for its holiday season, opening December 2. New works by Jamar Roberts and Yue Yin join company classics, including a Roberts premiere honoring Luther Vandross.

events.title: August Wilson's Seven Guitars
events.venue: Lincoln Center Theater, Mitzi E. Newhouse Theater
events.description: Ruben Santiago-Hudson directs August Wilson’s blues-inflected drama, now extended through January 17. Russell Hornsby, Kristolyn Lloyd, Roslyn Ruff, John Douglas Thompson, Daniel J. Watts, Michael Potts, and Chanté Adams bring Wilson’s Pittsburgh world to the stage.

events.title: New York Philharmonic: Rouvali Conducts Schubert
events.description: Santtu-Matias Rouvali leads the New York Philharmonic in a program featuring Florence Price’s Dances in the Canebrakes, orchestrated by William Grant Still, alongside Schubert.
events.venue: Wu Tsai Theater, David Geffen Hall

events.title: Armstrong in Ghana
events.dates: Now on view; closing date not announced
events.description: An archival exhibition explores Louis Armstrong’s travels to Ghana and the lasting connections between his music and the country’s cultural history.

events.title: Art of the Harlem Renaissance
events.dates: Now on view; closing date not announced
events.description: Augusta Savage’s portrait of Eugene Kinckle Jones and illustrated covers of Opportunity magazine illuminate the Harlem Renaissance within the museum’s permanent exhibition, Moving History Forward.

events.title: The Conversation
events.description: Joshua Henry and Julia Harriman star in their soul- and jazz-scored musical, with a book by Nick Green and direction by Kenny Leon. Now in previews, the production opens December 7.

events.title: The Gospel of the Harlem Renaissance
events.dates: Recurring Saturdays, 4 PM; see performance schedule
events.description: Created by Titus Walker; Ujamaa Black American Theater. A long-running independent production on Harlem in the 1920s and 1930s.

events.title: Wanted
events.description: Solea Pfeiffer and Liisi LaFontaine play Black twin sisters who pass as white in 1893 Texas, with Ledisi as their mother. Angelica Chéri and Ross Baum’s musical is directed by Stevie Walker-Webb and draws on Chéri’s family history. Opening night is November 8.

events.title: Ms. Blakk for President
events.description: Ato Blankson-Wood stars as drag performer and activist Joan Jett Blakk in Tarell Alvin McCraney and Tina Landau’s play with music. Directed by Landau, the production revisits Blakk’s 1992 presidential campaign and the work of Queer Nation Chicago.

events.title: The Free Black Women's Library presents SOFT AUTUMN: A Printmaking Workshop
events.venue: The Free Black Women's Library Reading Room, 226 Marcus Garvey Blvd
events.dates: Sun, Nov 29, 3–5 PM; confirm with organizer
events.description: Explore collagraph printmaking with leaves, lace, and other textured materials at The Free Black Women’s Library in Bed-Stuy. Registration is required; confirm the workshop date with the organizer.
events.price: $5; see registration page for any fees

events.title: the ripple, the wave that carried me home
events.description: Written by Christina Anderson, directed by Tiffany Nichole Greene. A family that fought to integrate 1960s Kansas swimming pools, and the daughter who must honor that legacy.

events.title: Film Screening: 14TH
events.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, 515 Malcolm X Blvd
events.description: The Schomburg screens Ava DuVernay’s 14TH, a documentary examining citizenship, equality, and the Fourteenth Amendment. A discussion follows the screening.
events.price: Free; registration currently full—check for released places

events.title: BEMBÉ: The Feast of the King's Eyes
events.description: Roque Boa Morte’s photographs document Bembé do Mercado, the Afro-Brazilian celebration held in Santo Amaro, Bahia, since 1889. Jamile Borges organizes the exhibition for Black Awareness Month.
events.venue: Consulate General of Brazil in New York, 225 East 41st Street

events.title: A Very SW!NG OUT Holiday
events.discipline: Dance / Lindy Hop and live jazz
events.description: LaTasha Barnes joins the creative team behind this holiday celebration of Lindy Hop, created by Caleb Teicher and collaborators. The Eyal Vilner Big Band supplies live music, and audiences can join an onstage dance jam.

events.title: Black America: The Last 10 Years
events.venue: CUNY Graduate Center, Elebash Recital Hall
events.description: Carol Jenkins with Kimberlé Crenshaw, Trymaine Lee, Nell Irvin Painter, Frederick Joseph. CUNY TV's Black America marks ten years with historian and painter Nell Irvin Painter and Kimberlé Crenshaw.

events.title: HUMAN
events.description: Nehprii Amenii, music by Martha Redbone and Aaron Whitby. Amenii's BAM debut.

events.title: Black Brilliance: An American Chronicle
events.discipline: Literature / library exhibition and visual art
events.description: Around ninety books and printed works trace two centuries of Black writing and publishing in America, including first editions and inscribed copies.

events.title: Conversations in Black Freedom Studies: Music is the Revolution
events.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
events.description: Soyica Diggs Colbert, Mary D. Williams, Quito Swan, and Jibola Fagbamiye discuss new books on Black music and liberation, from Mahalia Jackson and Nina Simone to Fela and dancehall.
events.price: Free; sold out—check for released places

events.title: Billie and Beyond featuring Victory Boyd
events.venue: The Billie Holiday Theatre, 1368 Fulton Street
events.dates: Fri, Dec 4, 8–9:30 PM; lobby opens 7:50 PM
events.description: Victory Boyd headlines the Billie’s music series, with an opening set by BATLA, a fifteen-member women’s percussion ensemble. Shanelle Gabriel and DJ Ty-Michelle host an evening inspired by Billie Holiday’s artistry and activism.
events.price: $25 through Nov 29; $35 from Nov 30 and at the door

events.title: Jenůfa — Kevin Short and Jazmine Saunders
events.description: Kevin Short sings the Mayor and Jazmine Saunders sings Jana in Janáček’s Jenůfa, led by Asmik Grigorian and Nina Stemme. Remaining performances are November 28 and 30, and December 4.
events.price: From $33 including fees; varies by performance and seat

events.title: Minor Music at the End of the World
events.description: Saidiya Hartman’s multidisciplinary work brings André Holland and Okwui Okpokwasili to the BAM Harvey Theater for its U.S. premiere.

events.title: S*an D. Henry-Smith and julie ezelle patton
events.venue: The Poetry Project, St. Mark's Church in-the-Bowery
events.description: S*an D. Henry-Smith and julie ezelle patton share poetry that moves across language, sound, image, and performance at the Poetry Project.

events.title: A Night of Inspiration
events.venue: Carnegie Hall, Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage
events.description: Ray Chew and Vivian Scott Chew bring gospel and orchestral music to Carnegie Hall, with Regina Belle, Jekalyn Carr, Donald Lawrence, Jonathan McReynolds, and Avery Sunshine among the announced artists. The evening honors Shirley Caesar and Richard Smallwood.

events.title: sonia louise davis: a promise, a portal, possibility
events.description: sonia louise davis brings tufted paintings, a steel sculptural instrument, neon, and wall text together in an exhibition shaped by improvisation, movement, and the possibilities of freedom.

events.title: To Uncover and Reveal to the World: Arturo Schomburg's Library
events.discipline: Visual art / library exhibition and literature
events.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
events.description: Curated by Laura E. Helton; more than 100 objects from Schomburg's 1926 collection. The books and manuscripts that founded the Schomburg, many shown for the first time, in its centennial year.

events.title: The High Low: A Night of Blues on Broadway
events.description: Wynton Marsalis organizes a free evening of blues and jazz inspired by August Wilson’s Seven Guitars, with reflections from director Ruben Santiago-Hudson and scholar Robert G. O’Meally.

events.title: Lea K. Green Artist Talk: Karon Davis
events.venue: Studio Museum in Harlem, 144 W 125th St
events.dates: Tue, Dec 8; reception 6 PM, conversation 7 PM
events.description: Sculptor Karon Davis joins Thelma Golden to discuss storytelling, materials, and the emotional life of her work. A reception precedes the conversation at the Studio Museum in Harlem.

events.title: Seneca Village: A Story of Black Freedom and Manhattan Real Estate
events.venue: The Graduate Center, CUNY, 365 Fifth Avenue; Gotham Center for New York City History
events.description: Alexander Manevitz and public historian Cynthia Copeland discuss Seneca Village, the free Black settlement displaced by the creation of Central Park, and the relationship between Black freedom and Manhattan real estate.

events.title: [HOME] GOING
events.description: Zola Dee’s radio play follows a young girl from the Carolina Sea Islands to Reconstruction-era South Carolina. Josiah Davis directs this online presentation, developed through National Black Theatre’s I Am SOUL residency.

events.title: Elizabeth Stordeur Pryor: Something We Said
events.venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
events.description: Historian Elizabeth Stordeur Pryor discusses Something We Said, her exploration of Richard Pryor’s comedy, the language of race, and her relationship with her father.

events.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem: Screening and Conversation
events.venue: Urban Civil Rights Museum, 117 W 125th Street, 4th floor
events.description: Discover the voices of the Harlem Renaissance through Once Upon a Time in Harlem. Filmmaker David Greaves and producer Anne de Mare join a conversation after the screening; a reception follows.

events.title: Your Arms Too Short to Box with God — 50th Anniversary Concert
events.venue: Bruno Walter Auditorium, New York Public Library for the Performing Arts
events.dates: Thu, Dec 10, 1 PM and 6 PM; talkback after the 1 PM performance
events.description: The York Theatre, in association with PAC NYC, celebrates Vinnette Carroll’s gospel musical with two free concerts. Marchánt Davis directs a cast including Nick Rashad Burroughs and Aisha Jackson, with music direction by Jermaine L. Hill.

events.title: Black Trees: Witness, Injury, and Black Arboreal Futures with Maurice Wallace
events.venue: Martin E. Segal Theatre, The Graduate Center, CUNY
events.description: Maurice Wallace considers how Black literature and visual art have represented trees, tracing connections among witness, injury, and possible futures. Jonathan Gray introduces the lecture at the CUNY Graduate Center.

events.title: Caribbean Theatre Festival: Caribbean Calling, Roots and Resurgence
events.venue: The Billie Holiday Theatre, 1368 Fulton Street
events.dates: Fri, Dec 11, 6 PM; Sat, Dec 12, 7 PM
events.description: The Billie and Braata Productions present two evenings of Caribbean theatre, pairing Christin Eve Cato’s Beneath the Land of Cockpit Country with readings from established and emerging playwrights. A panel closes Saturday’s program.

events.title: The Magic Flute — Holiday Presentation
events.description: Morris Robinson as Sarastro, Jazmine Saunders as Papagena, and Nicholas Newton as the Speaker appear in alternating casts of Mozart’s holiday presentation. Julie Taymor’s production is performed in English and runs about 90 minutes. Check the cast for your selected performance, especially on dates with two shows.
events.price: From $33 including fees; varies by performance and seat
events.artist: Morris Robinson; Jazmine Saunders; Nicholas Newton

events.title: Michaela Yearwood-Dan: A Woman of Will
events.description: Michaela Yearwood-Dan explores Catholic imagery through a queer, feminist lens in new paintings, thirteen small apostle portraits, and ceramic-tiled benches made with Theodore Vass.

events.title: Steve Locke: I said what I said
events.description: Steve Locke brings painting, sculpture, and neon together in a show addressing Black and queer life, public memory, and the transatlantic slave trade. New Auction Block paintings anchor the exhibition.

events.title: Big Band Holidays
events.venue: Rose Theater, Jazz at Lincoln Center
events.dates: Dec 15–20, 2026; relaxed performance Dec 20 at 2 PM
events.description: Catherine Russell and Georgia Heers join the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra for holiday standards arranged for big band. Chris Crenshaw directs the music; Sunday’s matinee offers a relaxed performance.

events.title: Les Ballets Trockadero de Monte Carlo — Robert Carter’s Final Joyce Season
events.description: The Trocks return for three weeks of ballet and theatrical comedy. Robert “Bobby” Carter, known onstage as Olga Supphozova, has announced his retirement after this engagement, concluding thirty-one years with the company.

events.title: Verbal Description Tour: A Sustained Becoming
events.description: A guided verbal-description tour introduces work by Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, and Taylor Simmons in the Studio Museum’s artist residency exhibition. Designed for visitors who are blind or have low vision.

events.title: Centuries of the Black Press in America
events.description: Mark Whitaker, Frankie Hutton, and Alvin Patrick discuss the history of the Black press in a program accompanying Black Brilliance: An American Chronicle.

events.title: Art in Conversation
events.description: Artists D. Lammie-Hanson and Gina Athena Ulysse join public art historian Jeffreen M. H. Ash for a conversation on art and civil rights, moderated by museum director Jennifer Scott.

events.title: esperanza spalding: Carnegie Hall Perspectives
events.description: esperanza spalding opens her Carnegie Hall Perspectives series with an exploration of anthems, bringing New York jazz musicians and contemporary dancers together at Zankel Hall.

events.title: Beverly Buchanan: Ruination and Regeneration
events.description: Beverly Buchanan’s paintings and sculptural shacks draw on the rural roads and weathered buildings of Georgia, exploring the relationship between place, memory, and survival.

events.title: Chakaia Booker: Unpacked
events.description: Chakaia Booker transforms discarded rubber tires into sculptures that twist, fold, and weave industrial material into new forms. The exhibition spans three decades of her practice.

events.title: Heitor dos Prazeres: Abundant Existence
events.description: Paintings by Heitor dos Prazeres, the Rio de Janeiro artist and samba composer, celebrate dance, music, and everyday Black life in Brazil.

events.title: James Little: Homage El Shabazz
events.description: Six paintings from James Little’s Homage El Shabazz series honor Malcolm X through geometric forms in oil and wax. A book launch and signing with Aruna D’Souza takes place November 14.

events.title: Karon Davis: Wishful Thinking
events.description: Karon Davis’s sculptures consider the presence and absence of Black figures in art history, bringing questions of representation into the gallery.

events.title: Ludovic Nkoth: Between Lines
events.description: Ludovic Nkoth’s paintings of dancers and other figures examine the relationship between movement, discipline, and migration. The gallery is closed November 26–27 and reopens November 28.

events.title: Mary Lovelace O'Neal: Requiem
events.description: Paintings from the 1980s and 1990s trace Mary Lovelace O’Neal’s approach to abstraction, color, and Black experience, including work from her Race Women series.

events.title: Mildred Thompson: Cosmos Calling
events.description: Mildred Thompson’s abstract paintings draw on cosmic imagery, color, and movement, reflecting an artistic practice developed across Europe and the United States.

events.title: Robert H. Colescott: Cairo
events.description: Paintings made between 1964 and 1968 explore how Robert H. Colescott’s years in Cairo transformed his work and his understanding of Black identity.

events.title: 2026 Kweli International Literary Festival: Readings and Conversations
events.venue: Kweli; New York venues and online
events.description: Kweli’s festival continues with readings and conversations through December 10, followed by online craft talks and master classes through December 20. Explore fiction, essays, and poetry with established and emerging writers of color.

events.title: LaJuné McMillian: Child/ren of the Bloom
events.description: LaJuné McMillian brings motion capture and Black dance traditions into an exhibition exploring the connections between movement, identity, and technology.

events.title: Kehinde Wiley: What the Light Becomes
events.description: Kehinde Wiley’s new portraits begin with encounters on the streets of New York. Paintings, oil studies, and a film explore the lives of the city’s residents and the changing traditions of portraiture.

events.title: The Hip Hop Nutcracker — with Kurtis Blow
events.description: Kurtis Blow opens a New York City reimagining of The Nutcracker, with hip-hop dancers, a DJ, and a violinist performing to Tchaikovsky’s score. Jennifer Weber directs and choreographs the holiday production.

events.title: Celebrate Kwanzaa at Brooklyn Children's Museum
events.description: Brooklyn Children’s Museum opens its Kwanzaa celebration with Asase Yaa Cultural Arts Foundation. Families can join candle lighting, performances, and workshops in dance, drumming, and art.
events.price: Museum admission required; see ticket options

events.title: La Fanciulla del West — Joshua Blue at the Met
events.description: Joshua Blue sings Harry in Richard Jones’s new production of Puccini’s California Gold Rush opera. The ensemble also includes Travon Walker as Joe, Lonwabo Mose as Happy, and Harold Wilson as Ashby. Keri-Lynn Wilson conducts the run, which opens on New Year’s Eve.
events.price: From $33 including fees; varies by performance and seat
events.artist: Joshua Blue; Travon Walker; Lonwabo Mose; Harold Wilson

events.title: Our Friend, Jean: Early Works of Jean-Michel Basquiat
events.description: Jean-Michel Basquiat, from Alexis Adler's archive. Early paintings and ephemera at a Black-owned gallery.

events.title: Hank Willis Thomas at Ford Foundation Live Gallery
events.venue: New York Live Arts, 219 West 19th Street
events.description: Three works from Hank Willis Thomas’s Ex parte series revisit archival images of children pledging allegiance, considered alongside legal rulings on the incarceration of Japanese Americans.

events.title: A Sustained Becoming: Studio Museum Artists in Residence 2026
events.description: Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, Taylor Simmons. The first residency cohort to work in the museum's new building.

events.title: Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony
events.description: Arthur Jafa. The largest museum survey to date of a defining artist of Black visual culture.

events.title: Imitation of Life
events.venue: The Shed, Griffin Theater, with National Black Theatre
events.description: Lynn Nottage, John Legend, and Whitney White adapt Imitation of Life for the stage, with Adrienne Warren as Delilah. Co-produced with National Black Theatre, the musical is in previews and opens December 3.

events.title: Mark Bradford: Untitled (A–Z), 2010
events.description: Mark Bradford transforms found business advertisements into an alphabet of twenty-six works on paper. Layered and sanded surfaces connect individual letters with the social and economic life of the South Los Angeles neighborhoods where the materials originated.

events.title: Tone
events.description: Roy DeCarava, Gordon Parks, Lorna Simpson, Glenn Ligon, Kerry James Marshall, Ming Smith, Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, Zanele Muholi, and others; organized by Jayson Overby Jr. Photographs, paintings, and drawings built on black, white, and every gray between, opening with DeCarava.

events.title: Mix and Master
events.description: Dominique Morisseau, directed by Kamilah Forbes. A MacArthur Fellow's drama set in a Bronx record shop.

events.title: Sekou McMiller & Friends: Palladium Nights
events.discipline: Dance / Afro-Latin dance and live music
events.description: Sekou McMiller makes his Joyce debut with a celebration of New York’s Palladium Ballroom. Afro-Latin dance, jazz, and soul meet in a program with live music and an onstage jam after the performance.

events.title: Tosca — Kevin Short’s January Performances
events.description: Bass-baritone Kevin Short sings the escaped political prisoner Angelotti in Puccini’s Tosca. Aleksandra Kurzak and Piotr Beczała lead the January cast in David McVicar’s production. Short’s performances run on selected dates from January 6 through 29.
events.price: From $33 including fees; varies by performance and seat

events.title: We're Still Here: Quilted Works Curated by Carolyn Mazloomi
events.description: Fifteen artists from the Women of Color Quilters Network explore Black history and material culture in an exhibition organized by Carolyn Mazloomi, marking the network’s fortieth anniversary.
events.venue: Claire Oliver Gallery, 2288 Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Blvd

events.title: Thaddeus Mosley: Radial Forms, Early Work 1954 to 68
events.description: Early sculptures by Thaddeus Mosley reveal his approach to salvaged hardwood, balancing carved forms with the natural character of the material.

events.title: The Lost World: The Art of Minnie Evans
events.description: The Whitney surveys Minnie Evans’s visionary drawings, whose intricate patterns and imagined worlds draw on her Afro-Caribbean heritage.
events.venue: Whitney Museum of American Art, Floor 8

events.title: Christopher Myers: Unbound
events.description: Christopher Myers; 40-foot tapestries and stained-glass sculptures. Monumental tapestries answering book bans.

events.title: Incendiaries: The People's Flag Show 1970
events.description: Group exhibition including Faith Ringgold, alongside Jon Hendricks, Jean Toche, Yvonne Rainer, and 150+ downtown artists and activists. Revisits a landmark 1970 act of art-world protest against war, racism, and censorship, with Faith Ringgold's involvement central to the show's history

events.title: Rashid Johnson: Birthday Boys
events.description: Rashid Johnson explores fathers, sons, and shared birthdays through new mosaics, suspended sculptures, and a film. Birthday Boys brings questions of intimacy and inheritance to Hauser & Wirth’s Wooster Street gallery.

events.title: Coumba Samba: Stars and Stripes
events.venue: Whitney Museum of American Art, Floor 1
events.description: Coumba Samba, Senegalese American artist; guest curator Rujeko Hockley. A 26-year-old artist's first solo museum show, tracing uranium from African mines into the global nuclear order.

events.title: Calvin Royal III — vildwerk. Dancing for the Wild
events.description: Soirée Ambassador Calvin Royal III and Adji Cissoko perform Alonzo King’s Epilogue Pas de Deux from Deep River. The program brings dance and environmental conservation together.

events.title: Charlotte Ballet — featuring Mthuthuzeli November’s As I Am
events.description: Mthuthuzeli November’s As I Am brings ballet, contemporary movement, and African storytelling to Charlotte Ballet’s Joyce engagement. The evening also includes Alejandro Cerrudo’s Dos y Dos y Dos and Crystal Pite’s Solo Echo.

events.title: Carl E. Hazlewood
events.description: Carl E. Hazlewood, Guyana-born abstract artist and co-founder of Aljira. His second solo show at a Black-owned Bed-Stuy gallery, with two large works shown in New York for the first time.

events.title: Lisa Corinne Davis: What's Going On?
events.description: Paintings and works on paper by Lisa Corinne Davis bring maps, grids, and vivid abstraction into conversation with race, history, and cultural identity. The survey spans 2017–2026.

events.title: Lula Mae Blocton: Colors and Mirrors of Equality
events.description: Lula Mae Blocton explores color, geometry, and reflection in paintings shaped by her engagement with Black identity, equality, and lived experience.

events.title: Tschabalala Self: Tools of Worship
events.description: In her first solo exhibition with Petzel, Tschabalala Self uses found and repurposed textiles to construct figures that examine representations of Black women.

events.title: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026
events.description: Seventeen young artists in the Studio Museum’s Expanding the Walls program photograph New York’s streets, homes, and everyday encounters. Their images explore movement, stillness, and the experience of growing up in the city.

events.title: NYCB: Jennifer Archibald and Jamar Roberts
events.description: Jennifer Archibald’s Shared Rain and Jamar Roberts’ Foreseeable Future return in NYCB’s Contemporary Choreography II program, alongside works by Justin Peck and Christopher Wheeldon. February 6 has matinee and evening performances; February 27 is a matinee.

events.title: Geometries
events.description: Julie Mehretu, Alma Thomas, Jack Whitten, William T. Williams, and others. Black abstraction organized around geometry.

events.title: Grass — Daniel Kaluuya and Branden Jacobs-Jenkins
events.venue: Park Avenue Armory, Wade Thompson Drill Hall
events.description: Daniel Kaluuya makes his American stage debut in Branden Jacobs-Jenkins’s play about a mother and son traveling through the American South. Directed by Sarah Benson; co-commissioned with National Black Theatre.

events.title: Ronald K. Brown/EVIDENCE — Winter Season at the Joyce
events.discipline: Dance / contemporary and African diasporic dance
events.description: Ronald K. Brown/EVIDENCE returns with two repertory programs blending African and Afro-Cuban dance with contemporary movement. Grace appears in Program B on February 25, 26, and the February 27 matinee.

events.title: Dreams of This Future: The Collection of Peggy Cooper Cafritz
events.description: Nina Chanel Abney, Kerry James Marshall, Wangechi Mutu, Jennifer Packer, and others. A landmark bequest from a Black patron and arts educator.

events.title: New York City Ballet: Taylor Stanley Farewell
events.description: Celebrate Taylor Stanley’s New York City Ballet career at a special farewell performance featuring Balanchine’s Emeralds. Stanley joined the company in 2010 and became a principal dancer in 2016.

events.title: Calvin Royal III — Serenade after Plato’s Symposium
events.dates: Mar 4, 7:30 PM; Mar 6, 2 PM; Mar 7, 1 PM, 2027
events.description: Soirée Founding Ambassador Calvin Royal III performs in Alexei Ratmansky’s Serenade after Plato’s Symposium during American Ballet Theatre’s spring season. Explore the full season alongside these announced appearances.

events.title: Silent Night — Justin Austin at the Met
events.description: Baritone Justin Austin sings Lieutenant Gordon in Kevin Puts and Mark Campbell’s opera about the Christmas truce of 1914. Dalia Stasevska conducts the Met premiere, directed by James Robinson, with performances on selected dates from March 8 through April 3.
events.price: From $33 including fees; varies by performance and seat

events.title: Woody De Othello: Guardian Spirit
events.venue: Public Art Fund, Brooklyn Bridge Park, Pier 1 and Manhattan Bridge View
events.description: Woody De Othello, Miami-born artist of Haitian descent; curated by Jenée-Daria Strand. His first outdoor show in New York: bronzes and redwood totems drawing on the Central African nkisi tradition.

events.title: Manon — Jazmine Saunders at the Met
events.description: Soprano Jazmine Saunders appears as Poussette in Massenet’s Manon. Nadine Sierra sings the title role opposite Matthew Polenzani as the Chevalier des Grieux, with Yves Abel conducting. Saunders is scheduled for all eight performances.
events.price: From $33 including fees; varies by performance and seat

events.title: We be the luminous blues...
events.venue: Lenfest Center for the Arts, Columbia University
events.description: Adama Delphine Fawundu. Banners honoring Black Columbia luminaries including Zora Neale Hurston and Paul Robeson.

events.title: Hard Art
events.description: Frank Bowling, Mark Bradford, Peter Bradley, Ed Clark, Torkwase Dyson, Nikita Gale, and 35+ others. A major survey of Black abstraction from 1969 to today, with free admission.

events.title: Calvin Royal III — Apollo
events.description: Soirée Founding Ambassador Calvin Royal III appears in George Balanchine’s Apollo during American Ballet Theatre’s spring season. His two announced performances offer another opportunity to explore the company’s repertory.

events.title: Forging Ahead: Recent Acquisitions of Black Women Artists
events.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
events.description: 21 artists including Simone Leigh, Tschabalala Self, Nona Faustine, Firelei Báez. The Schomburg's largest show of contemporary Black women's art.

events.title: Dance Theatre of Harlem at New York City Center
events.venue: New York City Center, 131 W 55th Street
events.description: Dance Theatre of Harlem returns to City Center with Robert Garland’s Brahms Variations, works by Nacho Duato and George Balanchine, and a New York premiere by Matthew Rushing and Samantha Figgins.

events.title: Kapwani Kiwanga: BLEED
events.description: Kapwani Kiwanga. A major site-specific installation.

events.title: Otello — Deborah Nansteel’s Spring Performances
events.description: Mezzo-soprano Deborah Nansteel sings Emilia in the spring cast of Verdi’s Otello. Brian Jagde and Ailyn Pérez appear as Otello and Desdemona, with Michele Mariotti conducting. Nansteel’s performances take place April 11, 17, 20, 24, and 27, and May 1.
events.price: From $33 including fees; varies by performance and seat

events.title: Greg Tate Art Wall: Carib-Import #1
events.venue: MoCADA Ubuntu Botanical Garden, 48 Lafayette Avenue

news.detail: The new museum has prompted debate over its approach to narrative art and collecting. George Lucas and Mellody Hobson co-founded the institution.
meta: George Lucas, Mellody Hobson, Lucas Museum of Narrative Art

news.title: Fridman Gallery Presents Dindga McCannon Solo Exhibition, "Yesterday and Today"
news.summary: A second solo show for the "Where We At" Black Women Artists co-founder.
news.detail: Sustained gallery attention for a founding figure of a landmark Black women's art collective. Already featured and shared in the September 9 briefing's Top 5.

news.title: Lynda Roscoe Hartigan Named Smithsonian American Art Museum Director
news.summary: Hartigan becomes director of a Smithsonian unit holding significant African American art collections.
news.detail: New leadership at a museum with major Black-artist holdings, amid broader Smithsonian pressure. Already featured in the September 9 briefing.

news.title: Kennedy Center Ceiling Collapse Renews Push for Shutdown
news.category: Performing arts / institutional · Funding and Policy
news.summary: A section of the Grand Foyer ceiling fell September 4, cited as further justification for the Center's closure and renovation plan.
news.detail: Latest turn in a year-long politicization pattern at a flagship national institution. Already featured in the September 9 briefing; still relevant background for the Bunch resignation story.

news.title: Spoken word artist Lyrical Faith, ready for her debut album, says she wants to inspire
news.summary: Profile of the Bronx-raised spoken-word poet and Harlem Bomb Shelter co-founder ahead of her debut album.
news.detail: The profile follows an artist working within New York’s independent spoken-word and slam-poetry communities.

news.title: Dreaming Soca: Why Granville Straker was a Brooklyn music legend and a connection to home for so many
news.summary: Profile of a Caribbean-American music promoter and soca pioneer's decades-long role in Brooklyn's diaspora music scene.
news.detail: The story traces Straker’s contributions to Brooklyn’s Caribbean music community and the connections his work sustained across the diaspora.
meta: Granville Straker; Brooklyn Caribbean music community

news.title: Cassandra Wilson, Grammy-Winning Jazz Singer, Dies at 70
news.summary: The genre-bending vocalist and 2022 NEA Jazz Master died at her home in Jackson, Mississippi.
news.detail: Loss of one of modern jazz's most distinctive voices. Already featured and shared in the September 9 briefing's Top 5.

news.title: Kennedy Center Removes Beloved Joel Shapiro Sculpture ('Blue')
news.category: Public art / performing arts policy · Major Industry
news.summary: The 24-foot "Blue" sculpture, installed 2019, was dismantled without advance public notice.
news.detail: Continuing pattern of politicized decision-making over a flagship national arts institution's public face. Escalation of the federal-arts-politicization storyline Soirée already tracks via NMAAHC and the Smithsonian.

news.title: The Missing Colors of Black American Pigment-Making
news.summary: Examines Carver's overlooked pigment-making research and the absence of any dedicated archive of natural color-making by Black Americans.
news.detail: Recovers a scholarly gap in a canonical Black scientific-artistic figure's legacy. Strong BAC episode material; scholarship and archive angle.

news.title: Minnesota State Fair Removes Anti-Trump Crop Art After Artist Was Harassed
news.summary: An "8647" crop-art piece was removed at the artist's request after she was doxxed and threatened.
news.detail: A concrete instance of political art provoking real-world harassment severe enough to force removal. Free-expression pattern context; relevant to Soirée's ongoing censorship-tracking interest.

appointments.description: Golden will remain director and chief curator until a successor is appointed. The board has begun its search.

appointments.name: LaChanze
appointments.description: The co-founder steps down after four years as president. A successor has not yet been announced.

appointments.name: Lawrence Brownlee
appointments.role: Male Singer of the Year, International Opera Awards
appointments.description: The American tenor received the award at the November 21 ceremony in Vienna.

appointments.name: Cincinnati Opera’s Black Opera Project
appointments.role: Equal Opportunities Award, International Opera Awards
appointments.description: The project received international recognition for its work expanding opportunities for Black opera.

appointments.name: Nick Cave
appointments.description: Cave received a visitor-voted prize after the Biennale replaced its Golden Lions following the jury’s resignation and artists’ withdrawals.

appointments.name: Culture House Founding Playwrights Ensemble
appointments.role: Nine playwrights appointed to four-year terms
appointments.description: Reginald Edmund, Idris Goodwin, Cat Brooks, and Terry Guest are among the ensemble, with a guaranteed path to production.

appointments.name: 2026 Dance Magazine Awards Honorees
appointments.role: Recognition for artistry, education, and advocacy
appointments.description: The November 23 ceremony honored Ayodele Casel, Cleo Parker Robinson, Germaine Acogny, and others. Alicia Adams received the Lydia Joel Award; Eleo Pomare was honored posthumously.

appointments.name: Maren Hassinger
appointments.description: The award recognizes Hassinger’s sustained contributions to sculpture, performance, and installation alongside her BAMPFA retrospective.

appointments.name: Jennifer Scott
appointments.role: Founding Executive Director and Chief Curator, Urban Civil Rights Museum
appointments.description: Scott leads Harlem’s Urban Civil Rights Museum, which opened November 14 with exhibitions on Northern civil rights history and Harlem’s communities.

appointments.name: Laylah Ali
appointments.description: Ali is among fifteen recipients of an unrestricted $50,000 award supporting artists over forty.

appointments.name: Meg Onli and Zack Winokur
appointments.description: The Whitney curator and American Modern Opera Company co-founder will organize the Biennial opening in March 2028.

exhibitions.title: Armstrong in Ghana
exhibitions.description: An archival exhibition explores Louis Armstrong’s travels to Ghana and the lasting connections between his music and the country’s cultural history.
exhibitions.through: Now on view; closing date not announced

exhibitions.title: Art of the Harlem Renaissance
exhibitions.description: Augusta Savage’s portrait of Eugene Kinckle Jones and illustrated covers of Opportunity magazine illuminate the Harlem Renaissance within the museum’s permanent exhibition, Moving History Forward.
exhibitions.through: Now on view; closing date not announced

exhibitions.title: BEMBÉ: The Feast of the King's Eyes
exhibitions.venue: Consulate General of Brazil in New York, 225 East 41st Street
exhibitions.description: Roque Boa Morte’s photographs document Bembé do Mercado, the Afro-Brazilian celebration held in Santo Amaro, Bahia, since 1889. Jamile Borges organizes the exhibition for Black Awareness Month.

exhibitions.title: Black Brilliance: An American Chronicle
exhibitions.description: Around ninety books and printed works trace two centuries of Black writing and publishing in America, including first editions and inscribed copies.
exhibitions.discipline: Literature / library exhibition and visual art

exhibitions.title: sonia louise davis: a promise, a portal, possibility
exhibitions.description: sonia louise davis brings tufted paintings, a steel sculptural instrument, neon, and wall text together in an exhibition shaped by improvisation, movement, and the possibilities of freedom.

exhibitions.title: To Uncover and Reveal to the World: Arturo Schomburg's Library
exhibitions.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
exhibitions.description: Curated by Laura E. Helton; more than 100 objects from Schomburg's 1926 collection. The books and manuscripts that founded the Schomburg, many shown for the first time, in its centennial year.
exhibitions.discipline: Visual art / library exhibition and literature

exhibitions.title: Michaela Yearwood-Dan: A Woman of Will
exhibitions.description: Michaela Yearwood-Dan explores Catholic imagery through a queer, feminist lens in new paintings, thirteen small apostle portraits, and ceramic-tiled benches made with Theodore Vass.

exhibitions.title: Steve Locke: I said what I said
exhibitions.description: Steve Locke brings painting, sculpture, and neon together in a show addressing Black and queer life, public memory, and the transatlantic slave trade. New Auction Block paintings anchor the exhibition.

exhibitions.title: Beverly Buchanan: Ruination and Regeneration
exhibitions.description: Beverly Buchanan’s paintings and sculptural shacks draw on the rural roads and weathered buildings of Georgia, exploring the relationship between place, memory, and survival.

exhibitions.title: Chakaia Booker: Unpacked
exhibitions.description: Chakaia Booker transforms discarded rubber tires into sculptures that twist, fold, and weave industrial material into new forms. The exhibition spans three decades of her practice.

exhibitions.title: Heitor dos Prazeres: Abundant Existence
exhibitions.description: Paintings by Heitor dos Prazeres, the Rio de Janeiro artist and samba composer, celebrate dance, music, and everyday Black life in Brazil.

exhibitions.title: James Little: Homage El Shabazz
exhibitions.description: Six paintings from James Little’s Homage El Shabazz series honor Malcolm X through geometric forms in oil and wax. A book launch and signing with Aruna D’Souza takes place November 14.

exhibitions.title: Karon Davis: Wishful Thinking
exhibitions.description: Karon Davis’s sculptures consider the presence and absence of Black figures in art history, bringing questions of representation into the gallery.

exhibitions.title: Ludovic Nkoth: Between Lines
exhibitions.description: Ludovic Nkoth’s paintings of dancers and other figures examine the relationship between movement, discipline, and migration. The gallery is closed November 26–27 and reopens November 28.

exhibitions.title: Mary Lovelace O'Neal: Requiem
exhibitions.description: Paintings from the 1980s and 1990s trace Mary Lovelace O’Neal’s approach to abstraction, color, and Black experience, including work from her Race Women series.

exhibitions.title: Mildred Thompson: Cosmos Calling
exhibitions.description: Mildred Thompson’s abstract paintings draw on cosmic imagery, color, and movement, reflecting an artistic practice developed across Europe and the United States.

exhibitions.title: Robert H. Colescott: Cairo
exhibitions.description: Paintings made between 1964 and 1968 explore how Robert H. Colescott’s years in Cairo transformed his work and his understanding of Black identity.

exhibitions.title: LaJuné McMillian: Child/ren of the Bloom
exhibitions.description: LaJuné McMillian brings motion capture and Black dance traditions into an exhibition exploring the connections between movement, identity, and technology.

exhibitions.title: Kehinde Wiley: What the Light Becomes
exhibitions.description: Kehinde Wiley’s new portraits begin with encounters on the streets of New York. Paintings, oil studies, and a film explore the lives of the city’s residents and the changing traditions of portraiture.

exhibitions.title: Our Friend, Jean: Early Works of Jean-Michel Basquiat
exhibitions.description: Jean-Michel Basquiat, from Alexis Adler's archive. Early paintings and ephemera at a Black-owned gallery.

exhibitions.title: Hank Willis Thomas at Ford Foundation Live Gallery
exhibitions.venue: New York Live Arts, 219 West 19th Street
exhibitions.description: Three works from Hank Willis Thomas’s Ex parte series revisit archival images of children pledging allegiance, considered alongside legal rulings on the incarceration of Japanese Americans.

exhibitions.title: A Sustained Becoming: Studio Museum Artists in Residence 2026
exhibitions.description: Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, Taylor Simmons. The first residency cohort to work in the museum's new building.

exhibitions.title: Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony
exhibitions.description: Arthur Jafa. The largest museum survey to date of a defining artist of Black visual culture.

exhibitions.title: Mark Bradford: Untitled (A–Z), 2010
exhibitions.description: Mark Bradford transforms found business advertisements into an alphabet of twenty-six works on paper. Layered and sanded surfaces connect individual letters with the social and economic life of the South Los Angeles neighborhoods where the materials originated.

exhibitions.title: Tone
exhibitions.description: Roy DeCarava, Gordon Parks, Lorna Simpson, Glenn Ligon, Kerry James Marshall, Ming Smith, Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, Zanele Muholi, and others; organized by Jayson Overby Jr. Photographs, paintings, and drawings built on black, white, and every gray between, opening with DeCarava.

exhibitions.title: We're Still Here: Quilted Works Curated by Carolyn Mazloomi
exhibitions.venue: Claire Oliver Gallery, 2288 Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Blvd
exhibitions.description: Fifteen artists from the Women of Color Quilters Network explore Black history and material culture in an exhibition organized by Carolyn Mazloomi, marking the network’s fortieth anniversary.

exhibitions.title: Thaddeus Mosley: Radial Forms, Early Work 1954 to 68
exhibitions.description: Early sculptures by Thaddeus Mosley reveal his approach to salvaged hardwood, balancing carved forms with the natural character of the material.

exhibitions.title: The Lost World: The Art of Minnie Evans
exhibitions.venue: Whitney Museum of American Art, Floor 8
exhibitions.description: The Whitney surveys Minnie Evans’s visionary drawings, whose intricate patterns and imagined worlds draw on her Afro-Caribbean heritage.

exhibitions.title: Christopher Myers: Unbound
exhibitions.description: Christopher Myers; 40-foot tapestries and stained-glass sculptures. Monumental tapestries answering book bans.

exhibitions.title: Incendiaries: The People's Flag Show 1970
exhibitions.description: Group exhibition including Faith Ringgold, alongside Jon Hendricks, Jean Toche, Yvonne Rainer, and 150+ downtown artists and activists. Revisits a landmark 1970 act of art-world protest against war, racism, and censorship, with Faith Ringgold's involvement central to the show's history

exhibitions.title: Rashid Johnson: Birthday Boys
exhibitions.description: Rashid Johnson explores fathers, sons, and shared birthdays through new mosaics, suspended sculptures, and a film. Birthday Boys brings questions of intimacy and inheritance to Hauser & Wirth’s Wooster Street gallery.

exhibitions.title: Coumba Samba: Stars and Stripes
exhibitions.venue: Whitney Museum of American Art, Floor 1
exhibitions.description: Coumba Samba, Senegalese American artist; guest curator Rujeko Hockley. A 26-year-old artist's first solo museum show, tracing uranium from African mines into the global nuclear order.

exhibitions.title: Carl E. Hazlewood
exhibitions.description: Carl E. Hazlewood, Guyana-born abstract artist and co-founder of Aljira. His second solo show at a Black-owned Bed-Stuy gallery, with two large works shown in New York for the first time.

exhibitions.title: Lisa Corinne Davis: What's Going On?
exhibitions.description: Paintings and works on paper by Lisa Corinne Davis bring maps, grids, and vivid abstraction into conversation with race, history, and cultural identity. The survey spans 2017–2026.

exhibitions.title: Lula Mae Blocton: Colors and Mirrors of Equality
exhibitions.description: Lula Mae Blocton explores color, geometry, and reflection in paintings shaped by her engagement with Black identity, equality, and lived experience.

exhibitions.title: Tschabalala Self: Tools of Worship
exhibitions.description: In her first solo exhibition with Petzel, Tschabalala Self uses found and repurposed textiles to construct figures that examine representations of Black women.

exhibitions.title: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026
exhibitions.description: Seventeen young artists in the Studio Museum’s Expanding the Walls program photograph New York’s streets, homes, and everyday encounters. Their images explore movement, stillness, and the experience of growing up in the city.

exhibitions.title: Geometries
exhibitions.description: Julie Mehretu, Alma Thomas, Jack Whitten, William T. Williams, and others. Black abstraction organized around geometry.

exhibitions.title: Dreams of This Future: The Collection of Peggy Cooper Cafritz
exhibitions.description: Nina Chanel Abney, Kerry James Marshall, Wangechi Mutu, Jennifer Packer, and others. A landmark bequest from a Black patron and arts educator.

exhibitions.title: Woody De Othello: Guardian Spirit
exhibitions.venue: Public Art Fund, Brooklyn Bridge Park, Pier 1 and Manhattan Bridge View
exhibitions.description: Woody De Othello, Miami-born artist of Haitian descent; curated by Jenée-Daria Strand. His first outdoor show in New York: bronzes and redwood totems drawing on the Central African nkisi tradition.

exhibitions.title: We be the luminous blues...
exhibitions.venue: Lenfest Center for the Arts, Columbia University
exhibitions.description: Adama Delphine Fawundu. Banners honoring Black Columbia luminaries including Zora Neale Hurston and Paul Robeson.

exhibitions.title: Hard Art
exhibitions.description: Frank Bowling, Mark Bradford, Peter Bradley, Ed Clark, Torkwase Dyson, Nikita Gale, and 35+ others. A major survey of Black abstraction from 1969 to today, with free admission.

exhibitions.title: Forging Ahead: Recent Acquisitions of Black Women Artists
exhibitions.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
exhibitions.description: 21 artists including Simone Leigh, Tschabalala Self, Nona Faustine, Firelei Báez. The Schomburg's largest show of contemporary Black women's art.

exhibitions.title: Kapwani Kiwanga: BLEED
exhibitions.description: Kapwani Kiwanga. A major site-specific installation.

exhibitions.title: Greg Tate Art Wall: Carib-Import #1
exhibitions.venue: MoCADA Ubuntu Botanical Garden, 48 Lafayette Avenue
exhibitions.description: Francks Francois Deceus, Haitian American artist. A garden mural on Black immigrants in transit, on the wall named for the late critic Greg Tate.

exhibitions.title: Thriving! Harlem as Homeplace
exhibitions.description: D. Lammie-Hanson’s metalpoint portraits of family and neighborhood anchor the museum’s inaugural temporary exhibition, honoring Harlem’s communities and the places that hold their histories.

exhibitions.title: Michael Richards: Free F'All
exhibitions.description: Michael Richards. A tribute to the Tuskegee Airmen by a Black sculptor lost on 9/11.

exhibitions.title: Ragtime: Cakewalk in Pianoland
exhibitions.venue: The Morgan Library & Museum, 225 Madison Avenue
exhibitions.description: Music and printed materials trace ragtime’s development through figures including Scott Joplin and Ernest Hogan, drawing on the John Davis Collection of Early Printed Musical African Americana.

exhibitions.title: Courtyard Commission: Precious Okoyomon
exhibitions.description: Precious Okoyomon. A living forest of plants, sculpture, and sound, free to enter, from a Nigerian American artist and poet.
